question.prompt: In \(\triangle ABC\) we have \(AB = 25,\) \(BC = 39,\) and \(AC = 42.\) Points \(D\) and \(E\) are on \(AB\) and \(AC\) respectively, with \(AD = 19\) and \(AE = 14.\) What is the ratio of the area of triangle \(ADE\) to the area of the quadrilateral \(BCED?\)

solutions.explanation:
Write \([F]\) for the area of figure \(F\). Triangle \(ABE\) provides a useful intermediate comparison, because each area ratio can then use two triangles with a common altitude.

Triangles \(ADE\) and \(ABE\) have bases \(AD\) and \(AB\) on the same line and the same altitude from \(E\). By the base-times-height area formula,
\[
\frac{[ADE]}{[ABE]}=\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{19}{25}.
\]
Similarly, triangles \(ABE\) and \(ABC\) have bases \(AE\) and \(AC\) on the same line and the same altitude from \(B\). Hence
\[
\frac{[ABE]}{[ABC]}=\frac{AE}{AC}=\frac{14}{42}=\frac13.
\]
Multiplying the ratios gives
\[
\frac{[ADE]}{[ABC]}=\frac{19}{25}\cdot\frac13=\frac{19}{75}.
\]
Since \(D\) and \(E\) are interior points of the two sides, \(BCED\) is the part of \(ABC\) remaining after \(ADE\) is removed. Its area is therefore \(56/75\) of the whole. The requested ratio is
\[
\frac{[ADE]}{[BCED]}=\frac{19/75}{56/75}=\boxed{\frac{19}{56}},
\]
choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Compare areas using shared altitudes
